newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat erases gains in late-session selloff.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat erases gains in late-session selloff.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher but well below the intraday highs amid late-session selling by locals and small speculative players, traders said.
The late selloff appeared to be triggered after small sell-stops were hit. A lack of sizable buying helped compound the late slide, traders said.
July wheat was hit particularly hard by the market-on-close selling, and the KCBT/CBOT July spread narrowed by about four cents per bushel in the session's final two minutes.
"The light-volume rally that we had going just disappeared. Locals and specs tried to get out and the doorway wasn't big enough," a KCBT trader said.

KCBT wheat had been broadly higher until the late sag. Traders attributed the earlier support to short-covering ahead of Monday's USDA crop report and to concern about weather conditions in the HRW wheat belt.

KCBT wheat settled 1/2 to four cents per bushel higher, with May up three cents at $4.57 but well below the intraday high at $4.63-1/2. July closed up 1/2 cent at $4.34-1/2. Earlier in the session, July had been as high as $4.40.
